title: Mutation and aliasing
summary: Two names can point to the same object. Changing the object through one name changes what the other name sees.

sections.heading: Names are labels
sections.body: `b = a` does not copy a list. It gives the same list a second name. After `b.append(1)`, both `a` and `b` show the change, because there is only one list.

sections.heading: Copies, shallow and deep
sections.body: `a.copy()`, `a[:]` and `list(a)` make a new outer list (a shallow copy). The inner objects are still shared. `copy.deepcopy(a)` copies the inner objects too.

example.caption: Prints [[1, 9], [2]]: the inner lists are shared

sections.heading: `is` and `==`
sections.body: `==` asks whether two objects are equal. `is` asks whether they are the very same object. `[1] == [1]` is `True`, but `[1] is [1]` is `False`: two separate lists with equal contents.
